faq.a: Abdulghaffar represents Arabic عَبْدُ الْغَفَّار, meaning servant of the All-Forgiving.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdulghaffar?
faq.a: The name is Arabic and is a compound of عبد and a second element.
Yes. The underlying compound is عَبْدُ الْغَفَّار (ʿAbd al-Ghaffār).

faq.q: What is the root of Abdulghaffar?
faq.a: عبد is related to ع ب د; al-Ghaffār is related to غ ف ر (gh-f-r).
Abdulghaffar is a traditional Muslim personal name because it contains a compound invoking al-Ghaffār, a divine epithet in Islamic tradition.
This record does not establish Abdulghaffar as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; the compound's religious meaning is distinct from personal-name attestation in the text.

faq.q: What does Abdulghaffar mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, the name means servant of the All-Forgiving; the compound combines عبد with al-Ghaffār.
The supplied “ab-dul-ghaf-far” is an approximate pronunciation; local pronunciations vary.

faq.a: The record classifies the name as masculine, consistent with traditional usage; regional frequency data is not supplied.
